source.title: Relative Langlands duality for some strongly tempered spherical varieties
source.authors: Zhengyu Mao, Chen Wan and Lei Zhang
readSections: Independent reviewer read all 35 pages of the April 2025 author draft, including §§1–6, all proofs and references.
Selected arXiv 2310.17837v3 passages: p. 2 splitting assertion and p. 11 Table 3. Not a full reading of this older version.
Publisher abstract, bibliographic record and all public notes; subscription main text unavailable. Published notes add local-character/normalization discussion absent from the April draft.
source.version: Author-hosted April 2025 draft, 35 pages; distinct from arXiv v3 and the journal text

summary: The paper proposes BZSV period and relative trace comparisons and proves local fundamental-lemma and smooth-transfer results for six models at p-adic places; the unit fundamental lemma for Models 5–6 excludes residue characteristic 2. The independent review repairs definitions, source formulas and ownership, but imported proof leaves, the full Table 3 replacement, Model 6 normalization and journal collation remain open. Conjectures are propositions to formulate, never proved assertions.

items.name: BZSV quadruple data
items.statement: Over a field k with the split reductive groups specified, a quadruple is (G,H,ρ_H,ι), where H→G is an embedding of a reductive group, ρ_H:H→Sp(S) is an algebraic symplectic representation, and ι:SL₂→G commutes with H. The Hamiltonian construction is item 82 and the hyperspherical predicate is item 80; neither is implicit in these data.
items.note: Separate the algebraic datum from the characteristic-zero structure theorem and from the arithmetic form/quantization choices.

api.name: bzsvDatum_compat

api.name: bzsvDatum_transport

items.name: Structure theorem for hyperspherical Hamiltonian spaces (Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis–Venkatesh, Theorem 3.6.1)
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let M be a smooth irreducible graded Hamiltonian G-variety satisfying all five conditions of item 80. For x on its unique closed G×Ggr orbit, H=G_x and S the symplectic normal fibre, BZSV Theorem 3.6.1 gives a unique equivariant Hamiltonian isomorphism from M to Whittaker induction of S from (H,sl₂), carrying x to the basepoint and inducing the identity on normal fibres.
items.note: Read BZSV arXiv 2409.04677v1 §§3.5–3.6 including its proof. Its cited BB/Luna/Losev inputs are not decomposed here. §3.9 uses a different working construction over rings; do not assert this theorem over arbitrary global fields.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.
Distinguish the theorem’s actual field/representation/normalization range from the conjectural or omitted cases recorded in gaps.

items.name: Complete reducibility of finite-dimensional sl₂-modules
items.statement: For an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field K, every Lie submodule N of a finite-dimensional module M for sl(Fin 2,K) has a complementary Lie submodule N′. Classification is separate item 87; identifying the model with an algebraic symmetric power is item 84.
items.locator: §1.1, p. 2 and §1.2, p. 6 (used implicitly in the decompositions ⊕ ρ_k ⊗ Sym^k)
items.note: Exact model-algebra complement statement, not an already constructed algebraic-group decomposition.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.

items.name: The decomposition 𝔤 = ⊕ ρ_k ⊗ Sym^k and the symplectic representation ρ_{H,ι}
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, for a specified algebraic H×SL₂-action on a finite-dimensional Lie algebra 𝔤, form multiplicity spaces ρ_k=Hom_SL₂(Sym^k,𝔤), with evaluation 𝔤≃⊕_k ρ_k⊗Sym^k. For the adjoint action, Lie(H) embeds in ρ_0. An invariant nondegenerate symmetric form on 𝔤 induces alternating forms on odd-k multiplicity spaces, and ρ_{H,ι}=ρ_H⊕⊕_{k odd}ρ_k is symplectic. Arithmetic descent of these data is a separate obligation.
items.note: Requires the SL₂-group/symmetric-power adapter and equivariant pairing descent; no characteristic-p semisimplicity is assumed.

items.name: Anomaly-free hyperspherical data
items.statement: For a complex hyperspherical Hamiltonian G-variety M, let c₂=c₂^G(TM)∈H⁴_G(M,ℤ)⊗ℤ/2. It is strongly anomaly-free if c₂=0 and anomaly-free if c₂ is the reduction of β² for an integral β∈H²_G(M,ℤ). For its inducing datum this is equivalent to c₂(ρ_{H,ι})≡c₁(θ)² for an algebraic character θ:H→G_m (item 102). A geometric condition over an algebraic closure is not an absolute étale-cohomology condition over a local field.
items.note: Exact BZSV Definition 5.1.2; duality conjecture separated as item 83. The topology/equivariant Chern-class substrate is an explicit unresolved input.

api.name: anomalyFree_data
api.statement: Strong anomaly-freeness implies anomaly-freeness via β=0.

api.name: anomalyFree_compat
api.statement: A witness is an integral β with mod-2 square c₂, not merely a mod-2 class.

api.name: anomalyFree_transport
api.statement: Equivariant isomorphisms carry the tangent Chern class and witnesses compatibly.

tests.name: anomalyFree_test_1
tests.statement: A zero symplectic representation has c₂=0 and is strongly anomaly-free.

tests.name: anomalyFree_test_2
tests.statement: For V=χ⊕χ⁻¹ over a torus, c₂≡c₁(χ)² mod 2, so V is anomaly-free.

tests.name: anomalyFree_test_3
tests.statement: The standard SL₂ symplectic module has odd weight sum and no nontrivial group character, so fails the criterion.

items.name: Absolute anomaly criterion for a local metaplectic splitting
items.statement: Let F be a nonarchimedean local field of residue characteristic different from 2 and H≤Sp(V) an algebraic F-subgroup. If a character θ:H→G_m satisfies c₂(V)=c₁(θ)² in absolute H⁴_et(BH,ℤ/2), the metaplectic double cover of Sp(V)(F) splits over H(F) (BZSV Proposition 5.1.1). For other places BZSV footnote 36 states an analogue only after pushing out the cover to S¹. For a map ρ from another group, a splitting over its image requires this criterion for that image; a lift of its pullback alone is weaker.
items.note: The proposition does not by itself construct compatible adelic/rational splittings. Its Appendix E.3 proof is not read; G3. Replaces the unconditional global/image assertion copied from MWZ p. 3.

items.name: The global Weil representation and theta series of a symplectic space
items.statement: For a symplectic space V over k, a maximal isotropic subspace Y and a nontrivial character ψ of 𝔸/k, the Weil representation Ω_ψ of Sp̃(V)(𝔸) on 𝒮(Y(𝔸)), and for φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸)) the theta series Θ^φ_ψ(g) = Σ_{X∈Y(k)} Ω_ψ(g)φ(X), which is left-invariant under the rational points (through the canonical splitting over Sp(V)(k)).
items.note: The adelic cover, the Weil representation on the restricted tensor product of Schwartz spaces and the rational splitting are MP.4; theta series, their convergence and automorphy are MP.5. Restricting along H → Sp̃(V) needs the splitting item above.

items.name: The period integral P_Δ of a BZSV quadruple
items.statement: Assume the centres of G and Ĝ finite (otherwise one divides by the centre). For ϕ an automorphic function on G(k)\G(𝔸) and φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸)), Y a maximal isotropic subspace of the space of ρ_{H,ι}, P_Δ(ϕ, φ) = ∫_{H(k)\H(𝔸)} P_ι(ϕ)(h) Θ^φ_ψ(h) dh, with P_ι the degenerate Whittaker period (1.1). The dual period P_Δ̂(ϕ, φ) is defined in the same way for automorphic forms on Ĝ(𝔸) and φ ∈ 𝒮(Ŷ′(𝔸)), Ŷ′ maximal isotropic in the space of ρ_{Ĥ′,ι̂′}. For non-cuspidal ϕ these integrals generally diverge and need a regularisation, of which Zydor's gives examples; no general method is available. This defines a functional on a specified convergence domain and after choosing a compatible adelic splitting. Outside it, regularization is additional data, not the value of a possibly divergent integral.

items.name: Tempered Arthur parameters, factoring through ι̂′, and lifting
items.statement: Use a conjectural global Langlands parameter formalism as an explicit hypothesis. For j:Ĥ′×SL₂→Ĝ, an Arthur parameter Φ factors through j when, up to Ĝ-conjugacy, there is Φ_H:L_k×SL₂→Ĥ′ such that Φ(l,x)=j(Φ_H(l,x),x). The equality is in Ĝ after applying j; maps into different groups cannot be equated. Temperedness here means trivial Arthur-SL₂ part for Φ_H in the assumed Arthur formalism. A packet lifting is separate conjectural correspondence data.
items.note: No global Langlands group or general packet construction is supplied by a definition. ML.4 supplies known classical cases, not this unrestricted assertion.

items.name: Conjecture 1.1(1) (Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis–Venkatesh, Conjecture 14.3.5 and (14.26)): the period P_Δ
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let π be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation of G(𝔸). For every embedding ν : π → L²(G(k)\G(𝔸))_π, P_Δ(ϕ), ϕ ∈ Im(ν), is nonzero only if the Arthur parameter of π factors through ι̂′ : Ĥ′(ℂ) × SL_2(ℂ) → Ĝ(ℂ); then π is a lifting of an Arthur packet Π of H′(𝔸) (H′ the Langlands dual of Ĥ′), and if Π is tempered one can choose ν so that |P_Δ(ϕ)|²/⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ “=” L(1/2, Π, ρ_{Ĥ′}) · ∏_{k∈Î} L(k/2 + 1, Π, ρ̂_k) / L(1, Π, Ad)² for ϕ ∈ Im(ν), ⟨ , ⟩ the L²-norm.
items.note: A conjecture, recorded as the statement the roadmap formalises; “=” is made precise by the next item.

items.name: The meaning of “=” in the period conjectures
items.statement: To state an exact identity one replaces the local L-factors at ramified places by the local relative characters of the (conjectural) Plancherel decomposition (Sakellaridis–Venkatesh §17, BZSV §9), and adds Dedekind zeta values determined by G and H (in known examples the L-function of the dual M^∨ of Gross's motive of (G, H)) and a global constant determined by the component group of the global L-packet of Π (BZSV (14.26)); BZSV formulate the conjecture only for everywhere unramified representations. Package measures, local relative characters, zeta factors and the component constant as explicitly supplied normalization data; an unspecified quoted equals sign does not define a numerical theorem.

items.name: The Weil representation of a Heisenberg group and its theta series
items.statement: For a symplectic space W, the Heisenberg group H(W) = W × (centre) with the group law given by half the symplectic pairing, its Schrödinger model on 𝒮(Y) for a polarisation W = X ⊕ Y with central character ψ, the extension to the Jacobi group H(W) ⋊ Sp̃(W), the explicit action of unipotent elements, and the global theta series Σ_{X∈Y(k)} Ω(u)φ(X).
items.locator: §1.2, pp. 5–6 (through Gan–Jun §2.3.2); §5.1, p. 19 (Ω_{n,ψ}); Propositions 5.1 and 5.3 (through Kudla's notes)
items.note: Schrödinger models of Heisenberg groups are MP.0, Stone–von Neumann and the metaplectic extension MP.1, the explicit operator formulas MP.2 and theta sums MP.5.

items.name: The degenerate Whittaker coefficient P_ι; Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi periods
items.statement: For ι : SL_2 → G with nilpotent orbit O_ι of 𝔤, let U = {g ∈ G : lim_{t→0} ι(diag(t, t^{−1})) g ι(diag(t, t^{−1}))^{−1} = 1}. The character ψ gives a Weil representation Ω′_ψ of U(𝔸) on 𝒮(Z(𝔸)), Z a maximal isotropic subspace of the weight-one space of 𝔲 under Ad ι(diag(t, t^{−1})) (Gan–Jun §2.3.2), with theta series Θ^φ_{U,ψ}(u) = Σ_{X∈Z(k)} Ω′_ψ(u)φ(X); the degenerate Whittaker coefficient is (1.1) P_ι(ϕ, φ) = ∫_{U(k)\U(𝔸)} ϕ(u) Θ^φ_{U,ψ}(u) du (written P_ι(ϕ)). If O_ι is even (Gan–Jun §2.3) Θ^φ_{U,ψ} is a character of U(k)\U(𝔸) and P_ι is a Bessel period; otherwise it is a Fourier–Jacobi period.
items.note: Bessel and Fourier–Jacobi models of classical groups are in the pending candidate GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups; the general degenerate Whittaker coefficient attached to an arbitrary nilpotent orbit is not.

api.name: degenerateWhittaker_transport
api.statement: When the orbit is even, the weight-one space is zero and the theta kernel reduces to a character.

tests.name: degenerateWhittaker_test_3

items.name: The representation ρ̂_ι̂ of the centraliser Ĥ_ι̂
items.statement: Fix ι̂ : SL_2 → Ĝ in the class of O_ι̂ and let Ĥ_ι̂ be the neutral component of the centraliser of Im(ι̂) in Ĝ; the adjoint action of Ĥ_ι̂ × SL_2 on 𝔤̂ decomposes as ⊕_{k∈Î} ρ̂_k ⊗ Sym^k. Since the adjoint representation is orthogonal, ρ̂_k is symplectic for k odd, and (1.2) ⊕_{k odd} ρ̂_k = (⊕_j τ_j ⊕ τ_j^∨) ⊕ (⊕_i σ_i) with the σ_i distinct self-dual irreducible symplectic representations of Ĥ_ι̂ — those occurring an odd number of times. Define (1.3) ρ̂_ι̂ = ⊕_i σ_i.

items.name: Conjecture 1.5: the degenerate Whittaker period
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let π be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation of G(𝔸) and ν : π → L²(G(k)\G(𝔸))_π an embedding, and assume the Arthur parameter of π factors through ι̂ (π is a lifting of a global Arthur packet Π of H_ι̂(𝔸), H_ι̂ dual to Ĥ_ι̂) with Π tempered. Then one can choose ν so that |P_ι(ϕ)|²/⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ “=” L(1/2, Π, ρ̂_ι̂) / ∏_{k∈Î} L(k/2 + 1, Π, ρ̂_k) for ϕ ∈ ν(π).
items.note: The paper's new conjecture; the evidence it cites is Lapid–Mao (next item but one), Lapid–Rallis Proposition 4 for principal orbits of the Levis GL_n × GL_n, GL_n, GL_{2n} of GL_{2n}, SO_{2n}, Sp_{4n}, the relative trace formula comparisons below, and §6.

items.name: The exact form of Conjecture 1.5
items.statement: Explicitly one expects |P_ι(ϕ)|²/⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ = ∗ · c(Π) · ∏_{v∈S} l(ϕ_v) · L(1/2, Π, ρ̂_ι̂)/∏_{k∈Î} L(k/2 + 1, Π, ρ̂_k), with ∗ special values of Dedekind zeta functions, c(Π) a constant depending on the component group of the global L-packet of Π, S the ramified places of Π (including the archimedean ones) and l(ϕ_v) local factors; for a function field and Π everywhere unramified the product over S is absent. When O_ι is not regular the local twisted Jacquet module of ι is infinite-dimensional in general but expected to be finite- (even one-) dimensional for representations whose parameter factors through ι̂′, so l(ϕ_v) might be defined as a regularised Fourier coefficient of a matrix coefficient; the paper does not pursue this. This is a conjectural normalization specification, not a construction of the still-unspecified ramified local functionals.

items.name: The two relative trace formulas I(f) and J(f′)
items.statement: Let N′ be a maximal unipotent subgroup of H′, ξ′ a generic character of N′(k)\N′(𝔸) and K_{f′} the kernel of f′ ∈ 𝒮(H′(𝔸)). Put J(f′) = P_{Δ_1}(P_{N′,ξ′,1}(K_{f′})) with P_{N′,ξ′,1}(K_{f′})(y) = ∫_{N′(k)\N′(𝔸)} K_{f′}(n, y)ξ′(n) dn. For f ∈ 𝒮(G(𝔸)) with kernel K_f put I(f) = P_ι′(P_{Δ,1}(K_f)), where P_{Δ,1}(K_f)(y) = P_Δ(K_f(·, y)). Define these only on convergent test data or with a named regularization. The heuristic spectral formula (1.4) is the conjectural item 95.

items.name: The automorphic kernel of a test function
items.statement: For f a test function on G(𝔸) (modulo a central subgroup where needed), K_f(x, y) = Σ_{γ∈G(k)} f(x^{−1}γy), the kernel of the right regular action R(f) on L²(G(k)\G(𝔸)).

items.name: Conjecture 1.8 and its local form (Remark 1.9)
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): There should be a comparison between I(f) and J(f′). Precisely: with Z, Z_1 and Z′ the spaces whose Schwartz functions enter P_Δ, P_{Δ_1} and P_ι′, so that the distributions are J(f′, φ_1) and I(f, φ, φ′), there should be a local correspondence (f_v, φ_v, φ′_v) ↔ (f′_v, φ_{1,v}) between 𝒮(G_v) × 𝒮(Z_v) × 𝒮(Z′_v) and 𝒮(H′_v) × 𝒮(Z_{1,v}) such that at almost all p-adic places, with φ_v, φ′_v, φ_{1,v} the characteristic functions of the integral lattices, its restriction to Hecke algebras is a homomorphism of the Hecke algebras of G_v and H′_v, and I(⊗f_v, ⊗φ_v, ⊗φ′_v) = J(⊗f′_v, ⊗φ_{1,v}) whenever the local components correspond.
items.note: Such comparisons are usually proved by unfolding both sides into orbital integrals and proving a fundamental lemma and smooth transfer.

items.name: Special case 2 (Assumption 1.11): rank-one spherical varieties
items.statement: Assumption 1.11: ι is trivial, ρ_H = 0 and G/H is a rank-one spherical variety (Sakellaridis, Duke 170 (2021), Table 1). Then Ĥ′ = PGL_2 or SL_2, and (G, H, ρ_H, ι) satisfies Assumption 1.10 iff ρ_{Ĥ′} = 0; among the rank-one models exactly (1.5) (PGL_2, GL_1), (SO_{2n+1}, SO_{2n}), (Sp_4, Sp_2 × Sp_2), (G_2, SL_3) do not. For these, Δ_1 = (PGL_2, GL_1, 0, 1), Δ̂_1 = (SL_2, SL_2, Std ⊕ Std, 1) and J(f′) = ∫_{N′(k)\N′(𝔸)} ∫_{T(k)\T(𝔸)} K_{f′}(x, y)ξ′(x)^{−1} dy dx (T = GL_1 ⊂ H′ = PGL_2), Jacquet's Whittaker–Hecke trace formula (Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. 97 (1987)); Conjecture 1.8 is then an analogue of Sakellaridis's rank-one comparison, with standard rather than generalised Schwartz test functions. Remark 1.12: the case (PGL_2, GL_1) is trivial; (Sp_4, Sp_2 × Sp_2) essentially follows from Mao–Rallis (Duke 152 (2010)); for (SO_5, SO_4) the fundamental lemma is Zinoviev's.
items.note: Footnote 5: as varieties PGL_2/GL_1 ≃ SO_3/SO_2, Sp_4/(Sp_2 × Sp_2) ≃ SO_5/SO_4 and G_2/SL_3 ≃ SO_7/SO_6.

items.name: Theorem 1.13: fundamental lemma and smooth transfer for the duals of the six models
items.statement: At p-adic places the paper asserts smooth transfer for the six Table 1 models against SL₂ Kuznetsov, and the fundamental lemma for normalized unramified basic functions. For Models 5–6 the fundamental lemma assumes residue characteristic ≠2; this restriction is part of the theorem. Models 1–4 use factor |a|^((dim 𝒥+1)/2). For Models 5–6 the printed smooth-transfer factor is |4| times this; the Model 5 sign convention is repaired in E9 and the omitted Model 6/dyadic calculation remains G5. This extraction does not certify that unresolved part.
items.locator: §1.3.3, Theorem 1.13, p. 10 (proved by Proposition 3.3, Theorem 4.4 and Theorem 5.9)
items.note: Theorem 1.13 is decomposed by items 42–44,55–57,69–71. Local results do not prove the global period conjectures or archimedean transfer.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.
Distinguish the theorem’s actual field/representation/normalization range from the conjectural or omitted cases recorded in gaps.

items.name: The six strongly tempered models of Table 1
items.statement: The models (G, H = H_0 ⋉ U, Ĝ, ρ̂) with H_0 = PGL_2: (1) PGL_6, SL_6, ∧³; (2) GSO_8 × GL_2/GL_1, S(GSpin_8 × GL_2), HSpin_8 ⊗ Std_2; (3) PGSO_12, Spin_12, HSpin_12; (4) E_{7,ad}, E_{7,sc}, ω_7; (5) PGSp_10, Spin_11, Spin_11; (6) GSp_6 × GL_2/GL_1, S(GSpin_7 × GL_2), Spin_7 ⊗ Std_2. Here S(GSpin_n × GL_2) = {(g_1, g_2) : l(g_1)det(g_2) = 1} with l the similitude character. They are the models of Wan–Zhang (Memoirs AMS) whose reductive part has rank 1, all Whittaker inductions of the trilinear GL_2-model; in Models 2 and 3 the two choices of H, exchanged by an outer automorphism, correspond to the two half-spin representations.

items.name: The Killing form
items.statement: For a Lie algebra L over a commutative ring R, killingForm R L is the bilinear form (x,y)↦tr(ad(x)∘ad(y)), with the usual finite-free trace interpretation. Nondegeneracy under the characteristic-zero semisimple hypotheses is separate item 88.
items.note: For reductive groups the central radical does not obstruct the opposite-root pairings used for ξ on U. The former note demanding replacement of the form was not justified.

items.name: The parabolic P = MU, generic characters of U and the element Ξ
items.statement: In each model G has a parabolic P = MU with Levi M of type A_1 × A_1 × A_1; M acts on the characters of U with a Zariski open orbit, whose members are the generic characters; fix one, ξ. For Models 1, 3, 4, 5 the stabiliser of ξ in M is H_0 = PGL_2; for Models 2 and 6 it is GL_2 × GL_2/GL_1^diag, into which H_0 = PGL_2 embeds diagonally. There is Ξ ∈ 𝔲̄ (P̄ = MŪ the opposite parabolic) with ξ(exp X) = ψ(⟨Ξ, X⟩), namely (α_i the simple roots): Model 1 (type A_5, α_i = e_i − e_{i+1}): P from α_1, α_3, α_5 and Ξ = X_{−α_1−α_2} + X_{−α_2−α_3} + X_{−α_3−α_4} + X_{−α_4−α_5}; Model 2 (type D_4, α_4 = e_3 + e_4): P = GL_2 × (the parabolic of GSO_8 from α_1, α_3), Ξ = X_{−α_1−α_2} + X_{−α_2−α_3} + X_{−α_4}; Model 3: P ⊂ GSO_12 from α_1, α_3, α_5, Ξ = X_{−α_1−α_2} + X_{−α_2−α_3} + X_{−α_3−α_4} + X_{−α_4−α_5} + X_{−α_6}; Model 4 (E_7, Bourbaki labels): P from α_2, α_5, α_7, Ξ = X_{−α_2−α_4} + X_{−α_4−α_5} + X_{−α_5−α_6} + X_{−α_6−α_7} + X_{−α_1} + X_{−α_3}; Model 5 (type C_5, α_5 = 2e_5): P ⊂ GSp_10 from α_1, α_3, α_5, Ξ = X_{−α_1−α_2} + X_{−α_2−α_3} + X_{−α_3−α_4} + X_{−α_4−α_5}; Model 6: P = GL_2 × (the parabolic of GSp_6 from α_1, α_3), Ξ = X_{−α_1−α_2} + X_{−α_2−α_3}.
items.note: Model 2 is printed with 'Type B_n' for the D_n root system (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: The SL_2-embedding ι and the dual quadruples Δ and Δ̂
items.statement: Ξ induces ι : SL_2 → G with ι((1 0; 1 1)) = exp(Ξ); the centraliser of ι(T_{SL_2}) is M and H_0 commutes with Im(ι), giving ι : H_0 × SL_2 → G. In BZSV terms the models give the dual quadruples Δ = (G, H_0, 0, ι) and Δ̂ = (Ĝ, Ĝ, ρ̂, 1), where ι is attached to the Richardson orbit of U and 1 is the trivial SL_2-embedding.

items.name: Corrected Model 1 adjoint branching and the Table 3 obstruction
items.statement: In characteristic zero, for Model 1 (G=PGL₆, nilpotent Jordan type (3,3)), the commuting SL₂_H×SL₂_ι acts on the standard six-dimensional module as Std₂⊗Sym². Hence 𝔰𝔩₆≃Ad_H⊗Sym⁰ ⊕ (1⊕Ad_H)⊗Sym² ⊕ (1⊕Ad_H)⊗Sym⁴. Thus dim=3+4·3+4·5=35, rather than the 27 obtained from the printed three Ad_H terms. The other five rows are not imported as valid branching formulas; item 89 is their open computation.
items.note: E15 confirms the first row is false as a full Lie-algebra decomposition. Suppressed trivial summands might be irrelevant to selected L-factors, but the table does not state that convention. This does not refute its even-parity consequence.

items.name: Conjecture 2.1: the (G, H)-side for the six models
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let π be a generic cuspidal automorphic representation of G(𝔸). items.name: The theta series of ρ̂ on Ĝ
items.statement: With ρ̂ : Ĝ → Sp(V), Y ⊂ V maximal isotropic and Ω_ψ the Weil representation of Sp̃(V) on 𝒮(Y(𝔸)), given a verified adelic splitting compatible with rational points, Ω_ψ restricts to Ĝ(𝔸); (2.1) Θ^φ_ψ(g) = Σ_{X∈Y(k)} Ω_ψ(g)φ(X) for g ∈ Ĝ(𝔸), φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸)). items.name: Conjecture 2.3: the dual side for the six models
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let π be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation of Ĝ(𝔸) with central character trivial on A_Ĝ(𝔸) and ν : π → L²(Ĝ(k)\Ĝ(𝔸)/A_Ĝ(𝔸))_π an embedding. The period P_Δ̂(ϕ, φ) = ∫_{Ĝ(k)A_Ĝ(𝔸)\Ĝ(𝔸)} ϕ(g)Θ^φ_ψ(g) dg (ϕ ∈ ν(π), φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸))) is nonzero only if the Arthur parameter of π factors through ι : H_0(ℂ) × SL_2(ℂ) → G(ℂ); then π is a lifting of a global tempered Arthur packet Π of Ĥ_0(𝔸) = SL_2(𝔸), and ν can be chosen so that |P_Δ̂(ϕ, φ)|²/⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ “=” ∏_{k∈I} L(k/2 + 1, Π, ρ_k)/L(1, Π, Ad)².
items.note: The paper's Theorem 1.13 is offered as evidence for this conjecture. Remark 2.4 notes that the lifting from SL_2 to Ĝ can also be obtained by theta correspondences with the minimal representations of Kazhdan–Savin, Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry and Magaard–Savin.

items.name: The Kuznetsov relative trace formula of SL_2
items.statement: G′ = Ĥ_0 = SL_2, N′ its upper triangular unipotent subgroup, ξ′((1 x; 0 1)) = ψ(x); for f′ ∈ 𝒮(G′(𝔸)) with kernel K_{f′}, J(f′) = ∫_{N′(k)\N′(𝔸)} ∫_{N′(k)\N′(𝔸)} K_{f′}(n_1, n_2)ψ(n_1)^{−1}ψ(n_2) dn_1 dn_2, N′(𝔸) ≅ 𝔸 with the ψ-self-dual measure (vol(𝔸/k) = 1).

items.statement: For f′ = ⊗_v f′_v: J(f′) = ∏_v J^+_v(f′_v) + ∏_v J^−_v(f′_v) + Σ_{a∈k^×} ∏_v J_v(a, f′_v), the products over all places v of k.

items.name: The space C^∞_OI(F^×, c_+, c_−) of germs of orbital integrals
items.statement: For F non-archimedean with uniformiser ϖ, q = |ϖ|^{−1}, and c_+, c_− ∈ ℂ: the locally constant functions f on F^× with bounded support in F such that for some neighbourhood ω of 0, f(a) = c_+ ∫_{1+ϖ^m𝒪_F} ψ((x + x^{−1})/a) dx + c_− ∫_{−1+ϖ^m𝒪_F} ψ((x + x^{−1})/a) dx for a ∈ ω − {0}, with m > 0 so large that |2| > |ϖ^m| (for a near 0 the integrals do not depend on m). C^∞_OI(F^×) is the union over c_± and C^∞_OI(F^×, 0, 0) = C^∞_c(F^×). For fixed nonzero (c_+,c_−) this is an affine fibre of the germ-coefficient map, not a vector subspace. Bounded support in F may accumulate at 0 and is weaker than compact support in F×; the zero-germ fibre is exactly C_c^∞(F×).
items.note: ψ is unramified when trivial on 𝒪_F but not on ϖ^{−1}𝒪_F; da is ψ-self-dual.

items.name: The parabolic Q = LN of Ĝ and the dual orbit (Models 1–4)
items.statement: For Model 1 (resp. 3, 4) Q is the standard maximal parabolic of Ĝ whose Levi does not contain α_3 (resp. α_6, α_7); for Model 2, Q is the product of the Borel of GL_2 and the standard maximal parabolic of GSO_8 whose Levi does not contain α_4. The Richardson orbit of Q is the dual O_ι̂ of O_ι (Remark 4.1); for Models 1–4 it is even, so the degenerate Whittaker period is a Bessel period, whereas for Models 5–6 it is not even and the period is a Fourier–Jacobi period.

items.name: N as a degree-three Jordan algebra 𝒥
items.statement: In Models 1–4, N is identified with a Jordan algebra 𝒥 of degree 3: Mat_{3×3}, Asym_{4×4} ⊕ Mat_{1×1}, Asym_{6×6} and the 3 × 3 self-adjoint octonionic matrices respectively (Asym = skew-symmetric). 𝒥 carries a trace tr and a norm N_𝒥, and (Mao–Rallis, Duke 87 (1997), §2) products A · A and A × A with (A × A) · A = N_𝒥(A); the generic character of N(k)\N(𝔸) is ξ_N(A) = ψ(tr(A)).
items.note: Mathlib has only the Jordan identity (IsCommJordan); the split Albert algebra is planned in Tau Ceti LieHighestWeight Layer 8, but the cubic norm structures (trace, norm, cross product) of all four algebras are not planned.

items.name: Proposition 4.2: unfolding of I(f, φ)
items.statement: For f = ⊗f_v and φ = ⊗φ_v: I(f, φ) = ∏_v I^+_v(f_v ∗ φ_v) + ∏_v I^−_v(f_v ∗ φ_v) + Σ_{a∈k^×} ∏_v I_v(a, f_v ∗ φ_v), where f_v ∗ φ_v = ∫_{Ĝ(k_v)/A_Ĝ(k_v)} f_v(g^{−1})Ω_ψ(g)φ_v dg, I^±_v(f_v ∗ φ_v) = f_v ∗ φ_v(0, ±I) (I the identity of 𝒥) and I_v(a, f_v ∗ φ_v) = ∫_{𝒥(k_v)} f_v ∗ φ_v(a, A)ψ((tr(A) − N_𝒥(A))/a) dA.
items.note: Proved as Mao–Rallis Proposition 3 for Models 1, 3, 4; Model 2 by a similar argument whose details are skipped. The printed formula repeats I^+ and omits the product and the argument a in the last term (sourceIssues E3); the corrected form is stated.

items.name: Conjecture 4.3(1): the fundamental lemma for Models 1–4
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let n = dim 𝒥, v non-archimedean with ψ_v unramified, and f′_{0,v}, f_{0,v}, φ_{0,v} the characteristic functions of G′(𝒪_v), Ĝ(𝒪_v)A_Ĝ(k_v) and Y(𝒪_v) (so f_{0,v} ∗ φ_{0,v} = φ_{0,v}). Then I^+_v(φ_{0,v}) = J^+_v(f′_{0,v}), I^−_v(φ_{0,v}) = J^−_v(f′_{0,v}) and I_v(a, φ_{0,v}) = |a|^{(n+1)/2} J_v(a, f′_{0,v}) for all a ∈ k_v^×.
items.note: Proved in the p-adic case by Theorem 4.4(2) and Proposition 3.3(2). The paper proves the stated p-adic specialization through the local orbital-integral theorems; the full source formulation at other places is not thereby proved.

items.name: Mao–Rallis's orbital integral identity (Mao–Rallis, Duke 87 (1997), Theorems 1 and 2)
items.statement: For F non-archimedean, ψ unramified, 𝒥 as above with n = dim 𝒥 and |a| < 1: ∫_{𝒥(𝒪_F)} ψ((tr(A) − N_𝒥(A))/a) dA = |a|^{(n−1)/2} ∫_{𝒪_F^×} ψ((x + x^{−1})/a) dx, proved in coordinates A = ∏_{γ∈Π′_0} x_γ with Π′_0 = {α + β} ∪ Π′ ∪ {γ_1, …, γ_r} ∪ {δ_1, …, δ_r}, by their Lemmas 4 and 5 (pp. 332–334).
items.note: Imported: the fundamental lemma for Models 1, 3, 4 is Mao–Rallis Theorem 1, and the proofs of Theorems 4.4 and 5.9 adapt this computation.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.
Distinguish the theorem’s actual field/representation/normalization range from the conjectural or omitted cases recorded in gaps.

items.name: The linear dependence of tr − N_𝒥 on a coordinate
items.statement: In the coordinates used by Mao–Rallis, tr(A)−N_𝒥(A) is affine in each coordinate x_γ, hence equals x_γP_γ+Q_γ with P_γ,Q_γ independent of x_γ. Identify P_γ with the directional derivative of tr−N using a declared norm/trace-pairing convention. In the convention dN_A(B)=tr(A^♯∘B), it is tr((I−A^♯)∘B_γ); the exact translation of the printed A×A−I convention remains G4.
items.locator: §4.2, proof of Theorem 4.4, p. 18; §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.9, p. 28
items.note: Do not silently fix the source coordinate sign without the MR97 definitions. The vanishing/stationary locus is insensitive to an overall nonzero scalar, but the phase identity is not.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.

items.name: The elementary identity (4.2)
items.statement: Let F be nonarchimedean, ψ unramified and Haar measure ψ-self-dual, so vol(𝒪_F)=1. For m∈ℤ and b≠0 with |b|>q^(2m), ∫_{ϖ^m𝒪_F}∫_{ϖ^m𝒪_F}ψ(bxy) dx dy=|b|⁻¹. Integrating in y first gives vol(ϖ^m𝒪_F) times the indicator of its ψ-annihilator pulled back by multiplication by b.
items.note: Replaces Mao–Rallis's Lemma 4 in the germ computations of Theorems 4.4(3) and 5.9(3).

items.name: Theorem 4.4(1): the regular orbital integrals of Models 1–4 exhaust C^∞_c(F^×)
items.statement: For F non-archimedean and every f ∈ C^∞_c(F^×) there is φ ∈ C^∞_c(Y(F)) with I(a, φ) = f(a) for all a ∈ F^×.
items.note: Proof: for a_0 ∈ F^× and m large, take K ⊂ 𝒥(F) a small compact open neighbourhood of 0 with |tr(A) − N_𝒥(A)| ≤ |a_0| on K and φ = vol(K)^{−1} 1_{(a_0+ϖ^m𝒪_F)×K} (the normalisation is misprinted, sourceIssues E4).
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.
Distinguish the theorem’s actual field/representation/normalization range from the conjectural or omitted cases recorded in gaps.

items.name: Theorem 4.4(2): the fundamental lemma for Models 1–4
items.statement: If φ = 1_{Y(𝒪_F)} and ψ is unramified, then I^+(φ) = I^−(φ) = 1 and I(a, φ) = 0 if |a| > 1, I(a, φ) = 1 if |a| = 1, I(a, φ) = |a|^{(n−1)/2} ∫_{𝒪_F^×} ψ((x + x^{−1})/a) dx if |a| < 1.
items.note: Models 1, 3, 4: Mao–Rallis Theorem 1; Model 2 by the same argument. With Proposition 3.3(2) it gives Conjecture 4.3(1).
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.

items.name: Theorem 4.4(3): germs of the orbital integrals of Models 1–4
items.statement: For φ ∈ C^∞_c(Y(F)), a ↦ |a|^{(1−n)/2} I(a, φ) lies in C^∞_OI(F^×, c_+, c_−) with c_+ = I^+(φ) and c_− = I^−(φ).
items.note: Proof: if {0} × 𝒥 misses supp φ the function is in C^∞_c(F^×); if ±I ∉ A_0 + ϖ^m𝒥(𝒪_F) it vanishes near 0 (via P_γ); for φ = 1_{ϖ^m𝒪_F} ⊗ 1_{I+ϖ^m𝒥(𝒪_F)} Mao–Rallis's Theorem 2 argument with (4.2) in place of their Lemma 4 gives I(a, φ) = |a|^{(n−1)/2} ∫_{1+ϖ^m𝒪_F} ψ((x + x^{−1})/a) dx for a near 0.
acceptance: Verify the full source hypotheses and every explicit dependency before using this statement.

items.name: The Fourier–Jacobi datum of Spin_{2n+1}
items.statement: For n=3 or n=5, the two consumers in this paper, and a root α of Spin_{2n+1} let U_α = exp(𝔲_α) with a basis X_α. Let P_n = M_nU_n be the standard parabolic whose Levi is attached to Δ − {e_1 − e_2, e_n}, U′_n ⊂ U_n the abelian subgroup spanned by U_α for α ∈ {e_1, e_i + e_j : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n}, λ(u) the sum of the coordinates of u in U_{e_1} and U_{e_i+e_{n+2−i}} (2 ≤ i ≤ [(n+1)/2]) and U″_n = ker λ. Then U_n/U″_n is a Heisenberg group of dimension 2n − 1 with centre U′_n/U″_n, which gives a Weil representation Ω_{n,ψ} of U_n/U″_n on 𝒮(Y_n), dim Y_n = n − 1, with central character ψ ∘ λ, and theta series Θ^φ_{ψ,n}(g) = Σ_{X∈Y_n(k)} Ω_{n,ψ}(g)φ(X), a function on U_n(k)U″_n(𝔸)\U_n(𝔸).
items.note: The printed general-n assertion has not been justified for even n. Restrict the planned Fourier–Jacobi construction to n=3,5 and require the commutator form to be checked.

Y_3), Ω′_ψ its Weil representation, f ∈ 𝒮(Ĝ(𝔸)/A_Ĝ(𝔸)), φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸)), φ′ ∈ 𝒮(Y′(𝔸)): I(f, φ, φ′) = ∫_{N(k)\N(𝔸)} ∫_{Ĝ(k)A_Ĝ(𝔸)\Ĝ(𝔸)} K_f(g, u)Θ^φ_ψ(g)Θ^{φ′}_{ψ,N}(u) dg du, with vol(N(k)\N(𝔸)) = 1 and vol(Ĝ(k)A_Ĝ(𝔸)\Ĝ(𝔸)) = 1.

items.name: The polarisation Y = Mat_{1×1} ⊕ 𝒥 for Model 5 and the N-action on 𝒥
items.statement: ρ̂ is the 32-dimensional spin representation of Spin_11, with the one-dimensional weight spaces (±e_1 ± ⋯ ± e_5)/2. N_0 is the unipotent radical of the Siegel parabolic (roots e_i, e_i + e_j), Mat_{1×1} the lowest weight line (−e_1 − e_2 − e_3 − e_4 − e_5)/2 and (5.1) 𝒥 = Span{ρ̂(X)v : X ∈ 𝔫_0, v ∈ Mat_{1×1}}, spanned by the weights Σ a_ie_i/2 with one or two a_i = 1; 𝒥 = Asym_{6×6} is a degree-3 Jordan algebra, Y = Mat_{1×1} ⊕ 𝒥 is maximal isotropic, and 𝒥 ≅ 𝔫_0 by matching 𝔲_α with the weight space of lowest weight + α, so that conjugation gives an action (u, A) ↦ u.A of N on 𝒥.

items.name: Proposition 5.1: the Weil representation Ω_ψ on N (Model 5)
items.statement: For φ ∈ 𝒮(𝔸 ⊕ 𝒥(𝔸)) and (a, A) with a ≠ 0: (5.2) Ω_ψ(u_{e_1−e_i}(t))φ(a, A) = φ(a, u_{e_1−e_i}(t).A); (5.3) Ω_ψ(u_{e_i}(t))φ(a, A) = ψ((N_𝒥(A) − N_𝒥(atX_{e_i} + u_{e_i}(t).A))/a)φ(a, atX_{e_i} + u_{e_i}(t).A); (5.4) the same with e_i + e_j in place of e_i; and at a = 0: (5.5) Ω_ψ(u_{e_i+e_j}(t))φ(0, A) = ψ(−tr((tX_{e_i+e_j}) · A × A))φ(0, A), (5.6) Ω_ψ(u_{e_1−e_i}(t))φ(0, A) = φ(0, u_{e_1−e_i}(t).A), (5.7) Ω_ψ(u_{e_i}(t))φ(0, A) = ψ(−tr((tX_{e_i}) · u_{e_i}(t).A × u_{e_i}(t).A))φ(0, u_{e_i}(t).A). Equivalently (Remark 5.2) Ω_ψ(n)φ(a, A) = ψ((N_𝒥(A) − N_𝒥((n, a).A))/a)φ(a, (n, a).A) for the GL_1 × N-action (u_{e_1−e_i}(t), a).A = u_{e_1−e_i}(t).A, (u_{e_i}(t), a).A = atX_{e_i} + u_{e_i}(t).A, (u_{e_i+e_j}(t), a).A = atX_{e_i+e_j} + u_{e_i+e_j}(t).A.
items.note: Stated as an easy consequence of Kudla's Proposition 2.3 (Notes on the local theta correspondence).

items.name: GL_n nilpotent and odd-multiplicity example
items.statement: For n>3, let V=(χ⊗Sym^(n−3))⊕W with dim W=2, and let GL₁×GL₂ act on χ and W. The SL₂ orbit in GL_n has partition (n−2,1,1); its type-A dual has partition (3,1^(n−3)). The exact commuting-group decomposition is End(V)=End(Sym^(n−3)) ⊕ End(W) ⊕ (χ⊗W∨⊗Sym^(n−3)) ⊕ (χ⁻¹⊗W⊗Sym^(n−3)). End(Sym^(n−3))=⊕_{j=0}^{n−3}Sym^(2j). Consequently the odd multiplicity part is the hyperbolic pair χ⊗W∨ ⊕ χ⁻¹⊗W when n is even, and zero when n is odd; its odd self-dual symplectic residual representation is zero in both cases.
items.note: Replaces ambiguous Ad⊗∧² notation with End(V); the n=3 centralizer changes, so treat that Whittaker boundary separately. The proposed dual-pair/trace comparison remains item 98.

items.name: The non-special example: Sp_{4n} and the principal orbit of (GL_2)^n in SO_{4n+1} (§6.2)
items.statement: G = Sp_{4n}, Ĝ = SO_{4n+1}; P = MN ⊂ Sp_{4n} and P̂ = M̂N̂ ⊂ SO_{4n+1} are the standard parabolics attached to the simple roots e_{2i−1} − e_{2i} (1 ≤ i ≤ n), M ≃ M̂ ≃ (GL_2)^n. O_ι̂ is the principal orbit of 𝔪̂, viewed in 𝔤̂; it is not special. The neutral centraliser of Im(ι̂) is Ĥ = Sp_{2n}, the adjoint action of Ĥ × SL_2 on 𝔤̂ is Ad ⊗ Sym^0 ⊕ Std ⊗ Sym^1 ⊕ ∧² ⊗ Sym², and ρ̂_ι̂ = Std. The dual O_ι is the Richardson orbit of P, giving ξ(exp X) = ψ(⟨Ξ, X⟩) on N(k)\N(𝔸) with Ξ = dι((0 0; 1 0)), and P_ι(ϕ) = ∫_{N(k)\N(𝔸)} ϕ(n)ξ(n) dn.

items.name: Conjecture 6.2: the Sp_{2n} × Sp_{2n}-period
items.statement: Define the proposition with the following source prediction (no proof or axiom is asserted): Let π be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation of G(𝔸) and ν : π → L²(G(k)\G(𝔸))_π. P_{G′}(ϕ) is nonzero for some ϕ ∈ Im(ν) only if the Arthur parameter of π factors through ι̂ : Ĥ(ℂ) × SL_2(ℂ) → Ĝ(ℂ); then π is a lifting of a global tempered Arthur packet Π of SO_{2n+1}(𝔸) and ν can be chosen with |P_{G′}(ϕ)|²/⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ “=” L(1/2, Π)L(3/2, Π)L(2, Π, ∧²)/L(1, Π, Ad).

For f on Sp₄ₙ define J(f) using the G′ period in the first kernel variable and (N,ξ⁻¹) in the second, and J′(f) using (U,ξ′⁻¹) instead, as in §6.2. items.name: Proposition 6.4: P_ι and P_{U,ξ′} on representations with a nonzero Sp_{2n} × Sp_{2n}-period
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible discrete automorphic representation of G(𝔸) = Sp_{4n}(𝔸) and ν : π → L²(G(k)\G(𝔸))_π with P_{G′} nonvanishing on Im(ν). Then P_ι(ϕ) “=” P_{U,ξ′}(ϕ) for ϕ ∈ Im(ν); more precisely P_ι(ϕ) = ∫_{X_0(𝔸_S)} P_{U,ξ′}(ϕ(· ℓ̄(x)ν_0)) dx for a large enough finite set S of places, with ν_0 a Weyl element and ℓ̄(X_0) the subgroup of Sp_{4n} of Ginzburg–Rallis–Soudry (JAMS 12 (1999), (4.12)).
items.note: Restore Sp₄ₙ and finite product 𝔸_S, but retain G6: inspect GRS Theorem 2/proof, the representation class, vanishing conditions, large-enough S and the actual measure/operator before accepting this imported root-exchange claim.

items.name: Hyperspherical Hamiltonian variety
items.statement: Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, a smooth irreducible graded Hamiltonian G-variety M is hyperspherical if it is affine, its invariant rational functions Poisson-commute, the moment image meets the nilcone, the generic stabilizer in G is connected, and the grading is neutral as in item 81. The grading scales the symplectic form by degree 2.

api.name: hyperspherical_transport
api.statement: Coisotropicity is the vanishing of the Poisson bracket on invariant rational functions.

items.name: Neutral grading
items.statement: For x in the closed G×Ggr orbit and f=μ(x), H=G_x, the cocharacter of N(H)/H induced by the grading must lift to h in an sl₂ triple (h,e,f) (after invariant 𝔤≃𝔤*). The action λ↦(λ^(−h),λ) fixes x and acts by scalar λ on the symplectic normal fibre S at x. These are both conditions, not merely a degree condition on μ.

items.name: Whittaker Hamiltonian induction
items.statement: Given commuting H and an sl₂ datum in G and a symplectic H-space S in the BZSV characteristic-zero setting, form U from the positive grading and its Heisenberg quotient u/u_+. Put S̃=S×(u/u_+)_f with the affine HU moment map. The Whittaker induction is (S̃×_(h+u)* (𝔤*×G))/HU, the Hamiltonian reduction in (3.17); over a chosen invariant identification it has the model [S×_(h*)𝔤^e]×^H G. The symplectic structure, quotient, moment map and grading are part of the construction.

items.statement: For Models 2–6 compute the complete H₀×SL₂_ι character of Lie(G), retaining all trivial multiplicities, central summands and the distinction between dimensions of the group and representation. Prove evaluation isomorphisms and then extract only the odd multiplicity part required by Assumption 1.10. Table 3’s literal rows cannot serve as certificates.
items.note: Open computation G8, not a corrected table asserted without evidence.

api.name: branchingCertificate_compat
api.statement: Evaluation of the character at identity equals dim Lie(G), retaining central summands.

api.name: branchingCertificate_transport
api.statement: The odd-degree projection is extracted only after the complete character is verified.

items.name: Cubic Jordan norms and coordinate conventions
items.statement: On the four carriers Mat₃, Asym₄⊕k, Asym₆ and the split Albert carrier, specify the unit, Jordan product, cubic norm, trace pairing and adjoint A↦A♯, with (A♯)♯=N(A)A and A∘A♯=N(A)1 in the chosen normalization. For skew matrices the Jordan unit is a fixed symplectic matrix and the product/trace must be transported through its inverse; ordinary skew-matrix multiplication is not a Jordan product. Supply the source convention translating MR97’s dot/cross notation, rather than assuming its scalar identity is the standard product.
items.note: Reuse the 9/15-dimensional constructions already proposed by ExceptionalThetaCorrespondencesForG2 and the pinned Albert carrier. Generic cubic-norm ownership still needs coordination G9.

items.name: Compatible adelic splitting and unramified basic vectors
items.statement: For each of the six algebraic representations, choose and prove compatible local lifts to the metaplectic extension, their restricted product, agreement with the rational splitting and almost-everywhere invariance of the lattice characteristic function. Check the central quotient in Models 2,6. An unramified basic function is normalized with Haar volume of the compact equal to 1; for a compact K of arbitrary volume, convolution uses 1_K/vol(K).
items.note: Separate from the local odd-residue-characteristic splitting criterion; G3.

api.name: adelicSplittingDatum_transport
api.statement: Their restricted product agrees with the chosen rational splitting.

items.name: Self-dual and quotient measure data
items.statement: Choose a nontrivial additive ψ and the corresponding self-dual additive Haar measure; for unramified ψ normalize vol(𝒪_F)=1. On product coordinates use product measures. On global unipotent quotients use vol(U(k)\U(𝔸))=1, and specify rather than conflate this normalization with measures on reductive quotients and singular slices. Coordinate changes carry the absolute determinant.

items.name: Heuristic discrete spectral identities

The paper’s quoted equals signs suppress test-function dependence and constants; they are predictions, not literal scalar formulas for every test function.

items.statement: For fixed a≠0 in Model 5, under the N₁≃Y′ coordinate measure, ∫_{N₁(𝔸)} Ω(u)φ(a,0) Ω′(u)φ′(0) du = φ(a,0)∫_{Y′(𝔸)}φ′(Y)dY. Indeed N₁ fixes 0 in 𝒥 and acts on φ′ by translations. No free u remains on the right.

items.name: Schrödinger generator and polarization formulas
items.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field F with char(F)≠2, a symplectic space W=X⊕Y and ψ≠1, Kudla Lemma 2.2 gives ρ(x+y,t)φ(x₀)=ψ(t+⟨x₀,y⟩+½⟨x,y⟩)φ(x₀+x). Proposition 2.3 gives r(g)φ(x)=∫_(ker(c)\Y)ψ(½⟨xa,xb⟩−⟨xb,yc⟩+½⟨yc,yd⟩)φ(xa+yc)dμ_g(y), with the uniquely L²-normalized quotient measure, for row-vector block g=(a,b;c,d).

items.note: Read Lemmas 2.1–2.2, Proposition 2.3 and its proof through Lemma 2.4. Stone–von Neumann is cited there, not independently reproved in this review.

items.name: Anomaly criterion on the inducing representation
items.statement: For a complex hyperspherical datum, put V=(u/u_+)⊕S=ρ_{H,ι}. Then M is anomaly-free iff there is an algebraic character θ of H with c₂(V)=c₁(θ)² mod 2. If Ξ is the multiset of nonzero torus weights of V, this is equivalent to the sum of one weight from each ± pair lying in X*(T)^W+2X*(T); strong anomaly-freeness uses 2X*(T). Multiplicities are retained.
items.note: Read proposition and proof, including Proposition 5.1.6. Its external topological cohomology inputs and rational descent remain open G2/G3.

items.name: Pinned integral E₇ carrier and standard comodule
items.statement: TauCeti.E7Minuscule.groupScheme is the explicit toral-closure group scheme over ℤ inside GL₅₆, with matrix points over every commutative ring. For every commutative R its standardComodule on R⁵⁶ is the corestriction of the GL₅₆ comodule and is faithful. The cited files do not prove reductivity, identify the carrier as an independently defined simply connected E₇, or supply the symplectic form required here. Those interfaces must be imported/verified, not the carrier reconstructed.

items.name: Pinned type-B coordinate spinor lattice stability

routes.title: Metaplectic automorphic forms, Part II: algebraic anomaly criteria for splittings

The target is precisely BZSV Proposition 5.1.1 as corrected in item 6: an algebraic F-subgroup of Sp(V), a character θ whose square Chern class equals c₂(V) in absolute H⁴_et(BH,ℤ/2), and nonarchimedean residue characteristic different from 2 give a splitting. routes.title: Automorphic spectral theory and trace distributions, Part II: rank-one Kuznetsov orbital integrals
routes.brief: Import the kernel and discrete spectrum from AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.4/AS.6, automorphic spaces from AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.2, and Schwartz–Bruhat/self-dual Fourier analysis from AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0. Construct the SL₂ two-Whittaker relative distribution, its regular representative w_a and two singular orbits, and its product/sum unfolding with v ranging over places. Prove Proposition 3.3: realization of every compactly supported locally constant function on F× by regular orbital integrals, the normalized unramified basic-function calculation, and the two singular germ expansion with a sufficiently small cutoff. The fixed-coefficient germ fibres are affine; zero coefficients give C_c^∞(F×). Tests include determinant(w_a)=1, the distinct ± singular terms, conductor/volume changes and dyadic cutoff |ϖ^m|<|2|. This is a general rank-one supplier for RelativeLanglandsDuality and other transfer consumers, not a second ordinary invariant trace formula. routes.title: Relative Langlands duality: hyperspherical data, periods and six local comparisons
routes.brief: Plan the BZSV application only after its explicit supplier gates. Its distinctive objects are hyperspherical Hamiltonian data, anomaly predicates and proposed duality, the normalized/conjectural period statements, and the six model-specific relative orbital-integral calculations. Every conjecture is a definition of a proposition with supplied parameter, normalization and convergence data, never an axiom or a proved global theorem. Final local targets are Theorem 1.13 decomposed into Theorems 4.4 and 5.9 and the generic rank-one Proposition 3.3 imported from AutomorphicSpectralTheoryPartIIKuznetsov. At p-adic places prove smooth transfer; the basic-function fundamental lemma for Models 5–6 assumes residue characteristic different from 2. Retain the regular/singular factors and Haar conventions, use E9’s positive mixed phase in the Model 5 formulas, normalize compact averaging by reciprocal volume, and control the mixed and quadratic terms in the small-box proof. Do not assert the uncomputed Model 6 dyadic constant or the printed Table 3 rows. Rebuild the latter from full weight characters; Model 1 has multiplicities Ad,1⊕Ad,1⊕Ad and dimension 35. The §6 GL_n and nonspecial Sp examples are separate conjectural/conditional targets, with MR04/MR2010/GRS hypotheses supplied before use. Imports, never replanned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.0 for Schwartz/Fourier/measures, MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.0–MP.5 and its anomaly extension for Weil/theta/splittings, AutomorphicSpectralTheory AS.4/AS.6 and its Kuznetsov Part II for L²/kernels/germs, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 for known Arthur cases only, ReductiveGroups for algebraic groups/root data, SpinRepresentationsPartIIArithmeticModels for actual symplectic representations, the coordinated cubic-norm owner for Jordan algebras, LieHighestWeightPartIINilpotentOrbits for dual orbits and branching, and TwistedAutomorphicDescents for general Fourier coefficients/root exchange. The accepted GanGrossPrasad, JacquetRallis and unitary FriedbergJacquet candidates own their own period spaces and transfers; they are comparison consumers, not alternate proofs of these six models. Before activation resolve G1–G12, including all Hamiltonian/cohomological suppliers, all cited proof leaves, exact spectral normalizations and full journal collation.

coverage.signature: Let k be a global field and G a split connected reductive group over k. A BZSV quadruple is Δ = (G, H, ρ_H, ι) with H a split reductive subgroup of G, ρ_H a symplectic representation of H and ι : SL_2 → G a homomorphism whose image commutes with H; it determines a G-Hamiltonian space M_Δ (Ben-Zvi–Sakellaridis–Venkatesh (3.17)). Δ is hyperspherical if M_Δ is hyperspherical in the sense of BZSV §3.5.1, whose main condition is the coisotropic one: the field of G-invariant rational functions on M_Δ is Poisson-commutative.
coverage.decision: Compare the full field, group, measure and representation signature; concept hits alone do not discharge the item.

coverage.signature: Every hyperspherical G-Hamiltonian space is associated to a BZSV quadruple (G, H, ρ_H, ι).

coverage.signature: For a BZSV quadruple Δ = (G, H, ρ_H, ι), ι extends to ι : H × SL_2 → G and the adjoint action of H × SL_2 on 𝔤 decomposes as 𝔤 = ⊕_{k∈I} ρ_k ⊗ Sym^k with ρ_k representations of H and I ⊂ ℤ_{≥0} finite; the adjoint representation of H is a subrepresentation of ρ_0. Set ρ_{H,ι} = ρ_H ⊕ (⊕_{i odd} ρ_i); it is a symplectic representation of H. For a dual pair (Δ, Δ̂ = (Ĝ, Ĥ′, ρ_{Ĥ′}, ι̂′)) the same decomposition 𝔤̂ = ⊕_{k∈Î} ρ̂_k ⊗ Sym^k is made on the dual side.

coverage.signature: Δ is anomaly-free if ρ_{H,ι} is an anomaly-free symplectic representation of H (BZSV Definition 5.1.2 and Proposition 5.1.5). The BZSV duality is a conjectural duality between anomaly-free hyperspherical BZSV quadruples of G and of the dual group Ĝ; for dual quadruples Δ = (G, H, ρ_H, ι) and Δ̂ = (Ĝ, Ĥ′, ρ_{Ĥ′}, ι̂′), Ĥ′ = Ĝ_Δ is the 'dual group' of Δ, while H and Ĥ′ (and ι and ι̂′) are not dual to each other in general.

coverage.signature: If ρ_{H,ι} : H → Sp(V) is anomaly-free, the metaplectic double cover Sp̃(V) splits over Im(ρ_{H,ι}): the preimage of Im(ρ_{H,ι}) in Sp̃(V) is isomorphic to ℤ/2ℤ × Im(ρ_{H,ι}). Composing ρ_{H,ι} with the embedding Im(ρ_{H,ι}) → ℤ/2ℤ × Im(ρ_{H,ι}) gives a homomorphism H → Sp̃(V), so the Weil representation Ω_ψ restricts to a representation of H(𝔸) on 𝒮(Y(𝔸)) for Y ⊂ V maximal isotropic.

coverage.signature: Assume the centres of G and Ĝ finite (otherwise one divides by the centre). For ϕ an automorphic function on G(k)\G(𝔸) and φ ∈ 𝒮(Y(𝔸)), Y a maximal isotropic subspace of the space of ρ_{H,ι}, P_Δ(ϕ, φ) = ∫_{H(k)\H(𝔸)} P_ι(ϕ)(h) Θ^φ_ψ(h) dh, with P_ι the degenerate Whittaker period (1.1). The dual period P_Δ̂(ϕ, φ) is defined in the same way for automorphic forms on Ĝ(𝔸) and φ ∈ 𝒮(Ŷ′(𝔸)), Ŷ′ maximal isotropic in the space of ρ_{Ĥ′,ι̂′}. For non-cuspidal ϕ these integrals generally diverge and need a regularisation, of which Zydor's gives examples; no general method is available.

For ι̂′ : Ĥ′(ℂ) × SL_2(ℂ) → Ĝ(ℂ), ϕ factors through ι̂′ if, after Ĝ(ℂ)-conjugation, there is an Arthur parameter ϕ_{H′} : L_k × SL_2(ℂ) → Ĥ′(ℂ) of H′ with ϕ_{H′}|_{L_k} = ϕ|_{L_k} and ϕ(x) = ϕ_{H′}(x)ι̂′(x) for x ∈ SL_2(ℂ); the Arthur packet of G(𝔸) of ϕ is then a lifting of the packet of H′(𝔸) of ϕ_{H′}.
